about: W3 story voices, written by tools/voices/story-lines.mjs from the mission data (do not edit the missions part by hand). Every `say` line (with its `who`) of every campaign and Chronicle mission, and the lines of the staged scenes a mission plays, grouped in packs of at most ~300 KB. tools/voices/make-voices.py renders them with the cast's stock Kokoro voice and processing; the client finds a clip by storyHash(text) of the exact English line. `spoken` maps an on-screen line to a variant used only for the voice (the screen keeps its text).

spoken.It is following us! A Dune Wyrm, Command: It is following us! A Dune Wyrm, Commander. It will dive under tanks. Please never point it at me.
spoken.Relay site in view. Clear the Sunward gu: The relay site is in view. Clear the Sunward guards before the crawler rolls in.
spoken.Three raids beaten. The balloons rise fr: Three raids, all beaten. The balloons rise from a yard on the east rim. Burn it before Hale builds more.
spoken.Ford ahead. Go over in one group, Comman: The ford is ahead. Go over in one group, Commander. A thin line gets cut in the water.
spoken.West conduit is scrap! The crystals near: The west conduit is scrap! The crystals beside it have stopped fading.
spoken.The relay is dark. Fleet, report your po: The relay is dark. Fleet, report your power. Up by a third? Thank you.
spoken.The fleet has sent a salvage truck of Sc: The fleet has sent a salvage truck, full of Scrappers, Foreman. Let it reach the front.
spoken.I pay what I owe, Captain. A toll on ber: I pay what I owe, Captain. But a toll on my berth cores, I do not owe.
spoken.A Waystation! Shields mend three times f: Look at that Waystation! Shields mend three times faster beside it. My grandmother would be proud.
spoken.The centre oasis first, Wagon-master. Th: The center oasis first, Wagon-master. Then north or east, whichever guard is weaker.
spoken.Five minutes of daylight left. Two oases: Five minutes of daylight left. Hold two of the oases for one minute. Ride, Wagon-master!
spoken.Guardian machines? Out here? Foremen, fa: Guardian machines? Out here? Fall back to the camp, Foremen, and log everything you see.
spoken.That beacon has a tower. Watchers first,: That beacon has a tower. The Watchers first, so the Rangers can see what they shoot.

excluded.briefing: Briefing lines are read on the briefing card before Begin mission; voicing them would fetch a pack before the match starts (the lazy-load rule: nothing before Start). On-screen only.
excluded.debrief: Debrief lines are read on the result card after the match; not part of this pass. On-screen only.

lines.text: The Harvesters know their work, Commander. Alloy builds everything, so let them cut.
Pick a Harvester and raise a Supply relay near camp. It drinks from the old Lattice.
Supply relay online. Now take your squad to the Builder relay by the river.
It is waking! Four hundred years dark and it still knows its work.
Meridian camp. My lights failed the moment that relay lit. Shut it down.
Ashfall troops at the ford. Vanguards in front, Rangers behind, and stay in the circle.
They pushed us off the relay. Clear the circle and stand in it again.
I asked politely, Commander. I will not ask twice.
It is answering. Four hundred years asleep, and it is answering us, Commander.
Every light in the Ashfall camp just went out. The same second our relay woke.
The relay is steady. Strange, though. Why would our light put out theirs?
Movement on the road! One Ashfall scout, only looking. Your Vanguards can send it home.
Their first attack will take a few minutes. Use them: more Harvesters, then the Foundry.
Something has made a den on the south bank. Pack animals that spit acid. They stay close to it, so leave them be or clear it.
Acid Hounds! Their spit eats metal. Keep the Breakers back and let the Rangers shoot from range.
The den is clear. They were nesting on Builder crates: one hundred and fifty alloy, only a little chewed.
Foundry is hot. And Commander, look: when our relay lit, theirs went dim. Same second.
Ashfall is on the move. Meet them at the ford, where they must bunch together.
First Breaker rolling. Aim it at a crowd and keep Rangers away from its nose.
Their guns cover the far half of the bridge. Go over in one group, Commander, and do not stop on it.
You cross my river while your own camp stands empty. That is careless, Commander.
The bridgehead is down! The west bridge is ours, and it runs right past their back fence.
Ashfall holds the middle relay. Its energy is feeding their Foundry now.
Twelve minutes, Commander. Every minute they stand, they build more.
Keep the river. I have other camps, and less time than you think.
Two Ashfall scouts are testing our bank. The towers will greet them; keep building.
Pads stand beside all three roads. Crew the ones near the crossings before the first column.
The relay needs seven quiet stretches to tune. Hold every crossing and I will get them.
Meridian camp. You hold a river that is not yours. My columns cross on the hour.
Two stretches done and the relay is warming. Wading slows them, Commander. Hit them in the ford.
Scrappers come in crowds. A Breaker crew hits the whole crowd at once.
The sixth column crosses now, with Scorchers. I would rather you stood aside.
One more stretch! The relay is almost in tune. I can hear it.
Last column, and it brings Battle tanks. Anti-tank crews on the bridges, Commander.
Their gun is down. Put a tower of ours up there, and I can tune the relay under its cover.
Tower up. Now keep the relay for one minute while I tune it.
The relay is in the middle of the lake. The ford nearest our camp runs straight to the island.
The tower on the island can see the whole ford. Cross in one group and climb the ramp together.
That relay is mine, Meridian. Get off my island.
Ashfall is wading over from the far shore. Keep a few guns on the island.
The island relay is ours. Listen: every relay in the valley, humming on one line.
No river here, Commander. The walls north of camp are your only cover. Use them.
Right on schedule. Hold at the walls, then follow them home while they are weak.
Four towers up. Now the camp can look after itself while you go hunting.
That siphon is huge. It could run ten camps. Where is all the power going?
Commander, the beam from this one points straight up. He is feeding something in orbit.
Forty thousand sleepers ride above us. Their lights fail first. Leave my siphons alone.
Received, Commander. Forty thousand people will sleep warmer tonight. I will note the courtesy.
Three hundred alloy, loaded. Hale will count that loss, Commander. So will his sleepers.
Half his siphon line is down. He will throw everything at you now. Stay together.
Eleven minutes. His next wave will have Scorchers in it. Finish the siphons.
That is no Ashfall print, Commander. It is an old Builder war machine, and they woke it up.
The Iron Vanguard. Nine weeks to pull it out of a trench. It guards my siphons now.
It marks the ground before each burst. Stay out of the red. Hit it when its core opens.
Its armour is cracking! It fires sooner now, but the red on the ground still gives you the same time.
One third of its plating left. I had hoped that machine would last the season, Commander.
It is down! Poor old thing. When this is over I would like to see how it was put together.
Nine weeks of repairs, gone in minutes. I will add it to the account.
You have just made a cold night colder for people who never harmed you.
Enough! My riders yield, Commander. Name your terms.
Then we are even. I will not forget it, Commander.
So be it. My wells will remember.
The centre oasis is closest. Take it first, then choose north or east.
Nothing personal, Commander. My gardens need that light as much as yours.
The north oasis feeds my last siphon. Remove them.
East oasis is ours. Listen to it hum! And look, the Sunward wells just lost pressure.
Attack on our camp. Keep a guard at home; the oases will not hold themselves either.
Captain Sol. Every relay Meridian lights, we both lose power. A truce, until they are gone?
I do not like you, Director. But my wells are dropping. Agreed, for today.
Both columns are turning toward the centre oasis, Commander. Together.
Four minutes of daylight left. Two oases, one minute in a row. Now, Commander.
You are walking into a Wyrm nest, Commander. The Caravan rides around those. Then again, we never had your guns.
It is following us! A Dune Wyrm, Commander. It dives under tanks. Please never point it at me.
Tuned! Both oases are steady. I wish I knew why the others keep going dim.
One Ashfall scout on the dunes. It is looking at us, not the oases. Your guard can send it home.
Four crawlers, one road, raiders on every bend. Clear the bends before the crawlers arrive.
The first two crawlers are entering the canyon now. Two more follow in a few minutes.
The last two crawlers are in the canyon. Bring them home too, please.
The crawlers cannot fight back. Keep them behind the squad, please.
Meridian in my canyon. Outpost guard, down the road. Nothing gets through.
Raiders coming down from the north. Hold the middle bend until they break.
A Breaker on the north bend shells the road. Rush it before the crawlers come up.
Every raider I have, to the north mouth. Nothing leaves my canyon.
A crawler is badly hit! Medics to the crawlers, please.
The outpost is burning. No more raiders from that corner.
The crawlers are through the canyon. Now I can finish the tuning core.
The crawlers brought three Vanguards, a Breaker crew and a Medic. Use them on the outpost.
I am driving the crawler myself. Please do not let anything large shoot at me.
Both Pact armies are coming at once. Leave the crawler in camp until this wave breaks.
Two Pact towers cover the far bank of the ford. Break them, or take the east bridge.
Ford is clear! Crawler moving. Slowly. It only has one speed.
Crawler hull at half! A Medic would be very welcome right now, Commander.
The forest road is Caravan ground, Commander. The Pact says I must stop you. So I will.
Then the road is ours by force. The Caravan's relay stores are ours too: two hundred alloy.
A fair offer, and I remember fair offers. Two riders for the Pact's sake. The rest go home.
Relay site in view. Clear the Sunward guards before the crawler rolls in.
Core is in. Oh. Commander, the relays are not separate machines. It is one circuit.
Meridian, hear me. Children in my wagons carry water from wells your relays starve. Count them before you count our dead.
One circuit? Then my wells did not fail because of you. Hale told me otherwise. I will be asking him why.
A Pact scout in the trees, Commander. It came to look at the crawler. Show it the guns instead.
Economy first today, Commander. More Harvesters, a second seam, and guards for both.
Ashfall attack. They will go for the Harvesters. Pull them behind your towers.
The seam is ours. Good copper crystal. And these shards are fresh, Commander. New growth.
First charge is in and the relay is humming. Look at the seam: the crystals are growing!
The relays do not burn crystal. They grow it. The Lattice is a garden, Commander.
If that relay wakes, my siphons in the basin fail. Take their Harvesters.
Ashfall has the seam. That alloy is going to their Foundry until you take it back.
Violet coats on the north-west rim, Commander. They are watching the seam, and they are not Ashfall.
Veil Survey scouts. They came to this world before any of us. Leave them be. We have enough enemies today.
Ten minutes gone. Storm clouds on the north rim. Raiders heading for the home seam.
Four minutes to the storm. Every Harvester on the nearest deposit, Commander.
Quota banked! The Basin relay is awake, and the crystal fields are already thicker.
Ashfall scouts on the basin road, two of them. Let the guard meet them before they reach the Harvesters.
Rangers to the refinery, Commander. Whatever is coming will come for the copper.
The lights are rising over the east rim again. Big and slow, and coming this way.
Meridian camp. Your refinery feeds a relay that starves my fleet. My balloons will close it tonight.
There, over the rim! A balloon with a fire under it, drifting straight at the refinery.
Ember balloons. Our towers cannot aim that high. Rangers and Anti-tank soldiers can.
Research Anti-air guns at the Command core, and every tower will shoot at the sky.
Our Foundry crew drew a gunship from the Ashfall wrecks. A level 3 core can build Hawks for us.
Kites in front! Spotters. They count your guns for the balloons behind them.
The refinery is burning! Shoot the balloons down first, Commander. I can mend the rest.
You kept our alloy on the Ashen Line. I am collecting it tonight, Commander, from the air.
You returned our alloy once. I aim at the refinery, not at your people. That is all I can offer.
Three raids beaten. The balloons rise from a yard on the east rim. Burn it before Hale builds more.
My yard is burning. Noted, Commander. Two weeks of work, gone in one evening.
The yard is down! No more balloons tonight. And look, the cloth is Sunward silk.
Send a Ranger up the ramp first, Commander, then build on the hill.
My column is on the ridge road. Your hill will not stop me.
That is the last column, and the biggest. Keep the guns on the hill firing.
The ridge is ours. High ground wins fights before they start.
A troop truck is crossing toward the base. Shoot it before it unloads: the squad dies with the truck.
I am coming myself, Commander.
My machines are spent, Commander. I yield the field.
A debt, then. I will repay it.
Then I will not be taking orders from you.
You have about three minutes before the first wave. Towers east of the relay, Commander.
Here they come, both armies together. Hold the line at the towers.
The Pact says your relay dries my wells, Commander. Prove me wrong or stand aside.
Breakers on the ridge, shelling range in a moment. Sally out or they grind the towers down.
The circuit map is drawing! Every relay shares one line. Vale, send it to everyone. Now!
All camps, this is Meridian. Nobody stole your power. Look at the map we are sending.
I have seen it. It changes nothing. I need the power tonight, not the truth.
I have seen it. You returned our alloy on the Ashen Line, so I send fewer guns tonight. Not none.
The relay is cracking! Engineers on it, please, before the tuning breaks!
Director, I read that map. If it is true, I have been fighting the wrong camp.
Then stand aside, Captain. My last wave does not need you.
One minute, Commander. Everything you have, around the relay.
Tuning complete! The relay held. You held, Commander.
Two Pact scouts on the road, checking our towers before the siege. Let the towers answer.
Pads line the whole road, Commander. Crew the lower ones first. The column starts at the bottom.
Meridian. That plateau is not on your schedule. My columns will clear it by nightfall.
First reading! The lines bend south and west, toward the ash plains.
Second reading. They cross under the old Ashfall camp. Something is buried there, Commander.
A long Scrapper column on the road. Breaker crews where the road bends, please.
A Kite over the gorge. Ranger and Anti-tank crews can shoot it down. Breaker crews cannot.
Third reading. It is a Builder vault, and the Lattice keeps a key inside it.
I have counted your towers, Commander. I am sending a tank for each of them.
Last column. Everything Hale has left on this road. Hold the top, Commander.
Balloons behind the column, the same as over the basin! Keep a Ranger crew near the top.
Squad is down. Nearest jammer is north of you, on the open ground. Quietly, Commander.
Four guards. They have not seen us. Breaker first, then Rangers, please.
That post has a Sentinel tower. It outranges your Breaker. Rush it with Vanguards or go round.
I am hit! Not badly. Fairly badly. A Medic, Commander, if one is free.
All three jammers are down. The vault is listening again. Take me to the door!
Door open. This one is ECHO, caretaker of the Lattice. You are the first to ask in 412 years.
The Builders did not fall. They left, and set the Lattice to sleep so the crystal could regrow.
A man in a grey coat took the Keystone key nine days ago. He means to draw all the power at once.
The whole camp is awake. Do not stand and fight, Commander. Get Okoro out the way you came.
Their depot is burning. Hale's next march will start a day late. Well done.
A Builder guardian. It is not asleep, Commander, it is waiting. The old door notes say it tests whoever comes.
It will not move unless we strike it. Your call. Order an attack on it if you want the test.
It is standing up. Commander, do not try to destroy it. Show it we can fight, and it should kneel.
Stop shooting! It is kneeling. I think we passed.
The guardian is walking with the squad. Keep it next to Okoro and let it take the hits.
We are out. And ECHO came with us. It is in my slate, counting my files.
My beacon is the gold light in the south-east. We can hold a while. Not a long while.
Captain Sol. A pact is a schedule. You broke it. I am sorry for what follows.
You came. You warned me and I did not listen. The Caravan pays its debts. We ride with you.
You came. You shared the forest light when you did not have to. The Caravan pays its debts twice.
You let me ride out of the dunes. I remember. The Caravan sends two hundred alloy and every Rider it has.
Hale's road to my camp runs under the dune plateau. Take the top, and his columns must climb to you.
The beacon is breaking! Commander, if it falls my people have no road home.
The shelling has stopped. Children are coming out of the wagons. Thank you.
Ashfall is hitting our camp too. He wants to keep us apart. Do not let him.
We hold the top. Keep the troops deep on the plateau: from the sand below they cannot see us.
You have met ECHO, I think. Then meet its Wardens. The key commands them now.
Those are the first patterns. Every unit on this world is a copy of them. This one is sorry.
Machines on your camp road! My second column is at the south road. It is yours.
The dunes are quiet. First time in a month. Where do we go next, Commander?
Their camp is down as well. Hale will have to find his fuel somewhere else.
That is the old one's nest. My grandmother named it. Five young ones guard it, and they bite hard.
The Elder Wyrm rides with you. In forty years nobody has tamed it. The Caravan will sing about this.
Ashfall scouts on the sand, two of them, looking for our camp. Let the guard see them off.
A truck with six soldiers is on its way to the front. They will meet you at the muster point.
The storm has turned against us. The Veil yields, Commander.
You are kinder than I was told. Thank you.
Then the Veil will not forget this.
The west and south dampers are a short march from camp. The centre one is the hard one.
Three armies, three directions. Towers on every side, Commander, and a reserve in the middle.
Our first camp stood here, Commander. One relay woke and the storm took it in a night. Please stop.
Archivist, that storm came because one relay woke alone. In tune, the Lattice makes no storms.
A machine would say so. I buried forty friends on this plateau. I cannot risk more.
Thank you. My crews are walking out now. I will remember who opened the door.
Then I cannot stop you. I can only ask the sky to stay clear.
Riders on the south road, Commander! Late, dusty and ready. Put us where it is worst.
The Crown is free. Stand in its circle for one minute and this one will tune it.
All commands: the plateau centre. They must not finish.
Tuning. Sixty relays are answering. Sixty-one. Hold the circle.
Fifteen minutes. Their siege corps has heavy machines now. Anti-tank soldiers to the front.
Sixty-four relays in tune. Look up, Archivist. The sky is quiet.
The Crown is lit and the sky is clear. No storm. In thirty years I never once saw that.
Warden sentries are probing the storm line, two of them. The towers will see to it.
Scout the ramps first. A Breaker below the rim can still reach the towers.
Intruders below the crown. Sending a patrol.
The crown is lost. Retaking it.
Get a tower up on the crown now, before their column climbs the ramps.
A troop truck is crossing toward the base. Shoot it before it unloads: the squad dies with the truck.
The clock is running, Commander. Build as you march. The middle conduit is nearest the ford.
Wardens and Ashfall together, on our camp. Hold with towers. The army keeps moving.
Ford ahead. Go over in one group, Commander. A thin line gets cut in the water.
One conduit cut. The draw is slower by a third. This one can feel the fields breathe.
Wardens, to the west conduit. Guard it with everything.
West conduit is scrap! The crystals near it have stopped fading.
You have cost me a day. I have forty thousand reasons to take it back.
Ten minutes left. Sol is sending you her reserve. Use it for the last conduit.
Four minutes. The oldest crystals are turning to dust. Please hurry, Commander.
The north conduit is dark. The Lattice is tired, but it is whole. Thank you.
Three conduits cut. My schedule has lost a day, Commander. The engine on the Keystone has not.
Ashfall scouts between the rivers, two of them. Hale wants to know how many we brought.
Pads and fields on all three roads, Commander. Crew the basin first, and send armour where the line is thin.
Echo counts the quiet in waves. Ten of them, and the southern relays are tuned for good.
Meridian. Every road to the keystone is mine until my fleet is fed. Stand aside.
Two waves down and the relays hum. Keep the roads shut, Commander.
Two Gunner teams from the Field workshop, Commander. Put them where the Scrappers bunch up.
Warden Rangers on the north road. Gunners pin them in the open, and your crews do the rest.
Halfway. A Gunner holds a whole column in place while it is shot. Nobody enjoys being pinned.
Walkers from the Wardens' yards lead this column. Bought, not borrowed. See how you like them.
Walkers outrange a Battle tank. Anti-tank crews, and flank them with armour.
Eight in tune. The Lattice is tired, but it is listening. Two more.
Last wave, and everything Hale has left. Hold the basin, Commander.
Two towers on the line and a squad behind them, Commander. Build up while it is still far away.
Ashfall crews are standing at three old relay posts. Whatever they wait for, it is coming from the north.
My Kite is over the north road. Whatever comes down it, we will see it first.
The relays woke with it. One sits south of the river, by the old pump: that one is the easy one.
There it is, coming down from the Keystone. Hale gave the Sovereign legs that walk, not just legs that stand.
Meridian. My Sovereign walks to your camp, and my relays carry its shield. Nothing you own can stop it.
That relay is failing. When the last one goes dark, its shield goes with it.
Last relay down! Its shield is gone. Everything on the Sovereign now, Commander.
Then it walks without a shield. It has walked through worse than you.
It has stopped! The core is running hot. New guns, Commander: a long rail and a ring of shells.
Same rule as before. Watch the red, step out, and keep shooting.
Half a Sovereign is still a Sovereign, Commander.
It is down, and it will not walk again. I am sorry, old machine.
My last walker. Very well, Commander. The Keystone will decide the rest.
A truck with six soldiers is on its way to the front. They will meet you at the muster point.
You spared my crews at the siege. Ashfall sends three hundred alloy. I am not a man who forgets.
You let me walk my crews out of the storm. The Veil sends two hundred energy, and my records.
Three armies will arrive inside four minutes. Towers and Rangers first. Nothing leaves camp yet.
Here they come, from three sides! Caravan, stand with Meridian. Not one step back.
The first offensive is broken. Now north, across the ford, to the engine.
My heavy wagons have arrived, Commander. Breakers and a tank. Spend them well.
Commander. The Veil has read Hale's engine for a week. Every reading says the same: it empties the Lattice.
Teo Lind, Veil Shades. Half my crews walked off his line this morning. The rest are watching what you do next.
Then let them watch. Every Shade who stands aside today is one gun fewer at the engine.
You spared the Archivist. Two of my Stalkers are yours, Commander. They shoot healers first.
Commander. You would do the same for forty thousand of yours. Do not tell me otherwise.
Director, tuned, the Keystone feeds your fleet for good. Your way feeds it for one year.
A year I can count. A promise I cannot. Wardens: their camp.
I watched the Crown light without a storm. All Veil commands: stand down. I was wrong.
You let my crews walk out of the dampers. Now I walk out of this war. All Veil commands: stand down.
Thank you, Archivist. I have unlocked your old camp records. Your friends are named in them.
Ten minutes of Lattice left. I can hear the far relays going quiet, one by one.
Four minutes, Commander. Forget the camps. Everything on the engine!
Every camp broken! You are thorough, Commander. I am glad we are friends now.
The engine is silent. Tuning the Keystone. One hundred and eight relays are answering.
Meridian towers on every road to the Keystone. It is ours to guard now, Commander.
The engine is silent. Tuning the Keystone for every camp. One hundred and eight relays are answering.
Four camps, one circuit. I can see the dunes glowing from here, Commander.
I can see every camp from here. All of them are lit.
Their scouts come first. Two Scrappers on the road. Let the towers take them; the armies come later.
The Harvesters are cutting, Foreman. A Salvage yard first: wrecks pay better than rock.
Yard standing. Every machine that falls near it is alloy for the fleet. Theirs and ours.
Riders on the plain. They come for the Harvesters. Let the towers greet them.
Director's people! Those wrecks lay in the sand for four hundred years. Nobody owns a wreck.
Captain Sol. My sleepers own it. Foreman, carry on.
Ten minutes. The fleet reports at the hour. I would like to tell them good news.
Keep your wrecks, Director. The dunes are ours, and we will remember the road you took.
Their camp is young, Foreman, and so are their towers. Strike before they learn the ground.
Meridian is answering. Hold at our bank, then cross while they count their losses.
Ashfall on our bank. Director, we took nothing from you. We only woke a relay.
Then you will not miss it, Commander. Foreman, proceed.
Both towers down. Into the circle, Foreman. One minute, and their light goes out.
They took the circle back. Clear it, Foreman. A schedule is a promise.
Twelve minutes. Their Foundry will be printing Breakers soon. Finish it.
They are shutting our relay down! Commander, it is going dark. Strange: their lights should come back now.
The relay is dark. Fleet, report your power. Up a third? Thank you.
First column in thirty seconds, Foreman. Crew the pads nearest the bottom of the road.
Ashfall towers on every bend. Director, we only want the vault records you took. Let us pass.
Commander, you want the Keystone. So do I. The difference is that I am counting forty thousand.
Heavy machines in the next columns. Anti-tank posts on the upper bends, Foreman.
The gorge held. The berth cores are safe for another month. Thank you, Foreman.
The bridge camp is nearest, Foreman. Cross at the south bridge and start there.
Riders on our road. It seems the Captain collects her tolls in person. Towers, please.
The fleet has sent a salvage truck of Scrappers, Foreman. Let it reach the front.
Director's Foreman! Every wagon on this road pays the Caravan. Yours too.
I pay what I owe, Captain. A toll on berth cores I do not owe.
Both camps are down. The Captain waits at the forest relay. Bring her to terms, Foreman.
Enough! The road is open, Foreman. Tell your Director the Caravan has paid its toll.
Let her ride home, Foreman. Ashfall keeps its debts as well as she keeps hers.
Eleven minutes. The cores are waiting at the river, Foreman, and so am I.
The road is ours and the Captain rode home. I would rather owe her a courtesy than a funeral.
The centre oasis is the nearest, and its pump is the most lightly guarded. Start there.
Scrappers on the dunes, heading for our wells. Keep a guard at camp, Wagon-master.
A Waystation! Shields mend three times faster beside it. My grandmother would be proud.
Caravan. These pumps run on a schedule that keeps forty thousand people alive. Leave them.
And my wells keep four thousand alive, Director. Every one of them a guest at my table.
Eleven minutes, and the water is still dropping. Faster, Wagon-master.
All three pumps are sand. Listen: the wells are filling again.
The centre oasis first, Wagon-master. Then north or east, whichever guard is weaker.
Captain Sol. We came to light relays, not to take your water. Can we talk?
You lit an oasis and my wells dropped the same hour. Talk is cheap. Water is not.
The north oasis feeds my last siphon, Captain. I will take it back.
Raiders on our camp. Half home, half on the oases. A caravan guards its wagons.
Captain Sol. Every relay Meridian lights, we both lose power. A truce, until they are gone?
I do not like you, Director. But my wells are dropping. Agreed, for today.
Five minutes of daylight left. Two oases, one minute. Ride, Wagon-master!
Two oases held. The wells are steady. And Hale owes me a truce. Interesting.
The south bridge is ours to cross. The road camp beyond it is the first to fall.
Meridian is on the road to our camp. They fight cleanly. So do we.
Captain, my towers hold the bridge as agreed. The road beyond is yours.
Both camps are ash. Now the relay, Wagon-master, before their crawler.
Sunward riders! Wait, please, listen. The core reads this relay and the river relay as one circuit.
When one wakes, the others dim. Nobody is stealing anyone's power. It is all one machine!
Fourteen minutes. Hale will ask why the road is still open. I would like an answer for him.
One circuit. If that engineer is right, every well we lost was lost to the same machine.
The battery is on the ridge, north of the wagons. Ride up the west slope, Wagon-master.
Captain Sol. A pact is a schedule. You broke it. I am sorry for what follows.
Scrappers on the wagon road! Riders to the circle, and keep the children's wagons shut.
Our wagon from the south wells is back, and full of Riders. Make room at the circle!
I am coming myself, Captain. Some accounts are settled in person.
Captain Sol, this is Meridian. Our Commander is on the road to you. Hold until noon.
The beacon is cracking! Wagon-master, if it falls my people have no road home.
Enough, Captain. My machines are spent. I yield the ridge.
Go home, Director. Count your sleepers, and tell them a Sunward captain let you walk.
The shelling has stopped. The children are climbing out of the wagons. Now, the Director.
The ridge is ours and the Director walks home. Meridian's dust is on the south road.
The middle rig is nearest the ford, Warden-prime. This one counts eight guards beside it.
Diggers are coming to your camp. Standing order two: guard what guards the Lattice.
A Pylon. The Builders made them to shield the buildings around them. You remember well.
Three rigs. Zero rigs. The Keystone is quiet again. Thank you, Warden-prime.
Guardian machines? Out here? Foremen, fall back to the camp and log everything you see.
They obey a key, the old records say. Then the key is worth more than the drills.
Twelve minutes. The drills are nine metres from the Keystone. Eight. Please hurry.
The south mast is a short march from your camp. The middle one stands beside the Crown.
Meridian machines, coming to your camp. They are copies of you, Warden-prime. Good copies.
Warden machines! Hale must have the key already. Commander, they are not fighting for themselves.
Understood. Stop them anyway, and save the readings. We need to know what the Crown is.
Both masts down. Now the Crown, guardians. Stand in its circle and let no one near.
The Crown is asleep under your feet. Sixty relays are asleep with it. This one counts them all.
Eight minutes. Meridian is learning faster than the grey coat. That is good. And not good.
The Crown is held. The key works, then. I had hoped I would not need to know that.
First column at the ford in thirty seconds. Crew the pads on the north bank.
Wardens on every crossing. ECHO, can you reach them?
This one is trying. Warden-prime: the grey coat is draining the garden. Count the crystals. Then decide.
Battle tanks on both bridges. Anti-tank posts at the far ends, guardians.
Juno here, on the south bank. I count the crystals with you. Twelve dark since dawn.
You held. Forty crystals by the river have gone to dust while you did. This one is sorry.
Two towers on the line and a squad behind them. Build while it is still far away, Warden-prime.
Diggers on the road to the Rise. Standing order two still holds: guard what guards the Lattice.
There it is, out of the north. Six legs, every one of them Builder work. Hale only taught it to walk.
It is one of the old machines, Warden-prime. It has no key either. It only has orders.
The relays woke with it. The south one stands by the old pump, alone. Start there, Warden-prime.
That relay is failing. When the last one goes dark, its shield goes with it.
Last relay down, and its shield is gone. Everything on it now, Warden-prime. The knees first.
Guardians, you were mine nine days ago. Stand aside, and the Sovereign walks past you.
This one counted your nine days, grey coat. They are over.
It has stopped! Half its plating is gone. Look at it, it is turning north.
Let it go. The Wardens do not chase. They guard.
Twelve minutes. The Sovereign is eleven hundred steps from the Rise. This one is counting them.
It turns home. Very well. Tomorrow it walks on Meridian instead.
The west beacon is closest, Surveyor. It has a tower. Let the Shades go first.
Teo Lind, Shades captain. Seven Shades, five Rangers, two Watchers, three Medics. All here, Surveyor.
They have not seen us. The Builders' records call this the quiet hour. Use it.
Our first camp stood here. One relay woke and the storm took it in a night. Please, be quick.
That beacon has a tower. Watchers first, so the Rangers can see what they shoot.
Who is on the plateau? Veil? You have cost me three nights of survey.
Director, a relay woken alone makes a storm. I have the record. Please read it.
Fourteen minutes. Dawn comes early on the plateau, Surveyor.
All three beacons are silent. The Crown sleeps. Come home, Surveyor.
Cross by the south bridge. The bridge mast is nearer, the road mast is better guarded.
Ashfall has noticed us. Towers by the camp, please. I would rather not lose the records room.
Our relay is up. It listens, it does not wake anything. That is the difference.
Both masts are down. Now the relay, Surveyor. One minute in its circle, and I will have the records.
Copying. The record names the river relay, the Basin relay, the Crown. It names them all as one.
Fourteen minutes. Meridian's crawler is on the north road. I want these records before it arrives.
One circuit. Every relay on Astra is one machine. Oh, Surveyor. That changes the storm.
The battery is at the plateau centre, beside the Crown. Towers by the dampers first, then go.
They are coming for the dampers. Hold the line, Surveyor. Every minute walks a crew home.
Riders, to the south damper! Gently. There are people inside.
Archivist. That storm came because one relay woke alone. In tune, the Lattice makes no storms.
I buried forty friends on this plateau, machine. I cannot risk more.
The battery is silent. Our crews can breathe. Now hold, Surveyor, until the last of them is out.
Nine minutes. The crews are out. Let them have the dampers now. I want to watch the sky.
The west mast is closest and lightly held. The machine sleeps by the middle one. West first, Surveyor.
Ashfall columns on the camp road. Keep a guard at home, Surveyor. The record room is all we have.
West mast in sight. They have not seen us yet. The Shades go first.
That mast is failing. Every one we break is a relay that will not be pulled awake tonight.
It is awake. Twelve metres of Builder iron. Out of the red, all of you!
Watch its core, Surveyor. The record says it opens after every burst.
Its plating is cracking. It fires sooner now, but the red still gives us time.
Veil? That machine cost me a month. You have chosen a strange night to wake up, Archivist.
I woke thirty years ago, Director. Tonight I am only keeping the sky quiet.
The second Vanguard is down. Four left in the record, and nobody has found them. Good.
Twelve minutes. Meridian cuts the draw in two days. I want these masts gone before then.
Both masts are silent. The draw cannot pull the plateau now.
